messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident PD-8732 fired — metering ingestion lag above alert threshold for billing pipeline. consumer-group: metering-aggregator-prod, lag: 12,400 msgs, avg processing ms/msg: 480. Severity: P1. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-8732

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-8732 assigned to sara_h_oncall (sarah). Escalation policy: metering-sre -> eng-sre.

sarah (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. quick check: are customers currently seeing token count mismatches? @shreya (customer-ops) pls advise.

shreya (customer-ops): We've received 3 support tickets mentioning delayed invoice previews and token counts off by ~5-10% for last hour. No billing blocks yet but customers are worried.

mike (eng-sre): I'm pulling offsets and tailing logs. Running: `kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server broker.prod:9092 --group metering-aggregator-prod --describe`

mike (eng-sre): Output snippet: `TOPIC metering-events PARTITION 8 CURRENT-OFFSET 1254000 LOG-END-OFFSET 1266400 LAG 12400` — partition imbalance, consumer instance metering-agg-2 is idle.

devex-ops: I see metering-agg-2 in CrashLoopBackOff since 02:14 UTC, OOMKilled in pod logs. Reason: spike in batching memory with seq_len=8192 on some requests.

mike (eng-sre): Repro: high-seq requests from public-api v2. Might be bad prompt sizes. Short-term: scale replicas and restart crashed pod. Command: `kubectl -n prod scale deployment metering-aggregator --replicas=6` then `kubectl rollout restart deployment metering-aggregator -n prod`

sarah (oncall): Doing scale+restart now. Also flipping consumer debugging to verbose to verify offsets after restart.

mike (eng-sre): Scale started. Watch: `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=metering-aggregator` — new pods coming up.

mike (eng-sre): Restarted metering-agg-2, pods stable. Re-checking lag. Running consumer describe again...

mike (eng-sre): New describe: LAG reduced to ~2,200 across partitions, processing ms/msg down to ~120. Throughput up.

lee (billing): If we stabilize within 30m can we avoid generating erroneous invoices? What window do we need to protect?

sarah (oncall): Good question. We should mark the affected ingestion window: 2026-03-14T01:10:00Z -> now. Plan: hold invoice generation for that window and run backfill recompute once the pipeline catches up. @lee — coordinate with billing to pause invoice jobs for affected customers.

lee (billing): I'll pause scheduled invoice batch for tonight's run for customers tagged with `billing: high-usage` and open a manual run after backfill. Notifying finance.

shreya (customer-ops): Notifying the 3 affected customers proactively — will say: we detected ingestion lag, counts may be stale; we're pausing invoice generation for affected window and will follow up.

mike (eng-sre): Raising follow-up: need to add a guard to drop very-large-seq events or route them to a slow-path to avoid OOM. Filed ticket INFRA-4123.

devex-ops: Fast mitigation done. New pods stable for 12m, lag trending to zero. Runbook we followed: /runbooks/metering-ingest-lag.md — note step about scaling and restarting crashed consumer.

sarah (oncall): Current status: degraded -> recovering. Customer impact: delayed token counts and invoice preview staleness for ~2 hours for a small subset of high-usage customers. No incorrect billed amounts yet (we paused invoicing).

mike (eng-sre): Starting backfill: kick off recompute job `python tools/recompute_window.py --start 2026-03-14T01:10:00Z --end 2026-03-14T03:30:00Z --target=s3://backfill-outputs/prod` — monitoring job queue.

sarah (oncall): Handoff in 2 hours to next oncall. If backfill isn't finished by then, please escalate. I'll update the incident ticket and send a postmortem stub.

shreya (customer-ops): Thanks — keeping customers updated. Will only mark resolved after recompute completes and billing confirms safe run.

pagerduty-bot: PD-8732 acknowledged by sarah. Status: acknowledged -> investigating.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Update: lag reduced to <200 after scaling. Backfill job queued (job id bf-764). Next check 1805123700.

sarah (oncall): Closing loop: mitigation in place, backfill queued, billing paused for affected window. Assigning postmortem to mike+lee. Tagging: priority-invoice, followup-infra. 

mike (eng-sre): Will write postmortem and propose fixed: hard caps on seq_len, better memory limits, and automated routing of large events.

lee (billing): After recompute, I'll validate token counts vs previews and approve invoices.

shreya (customer-ops): :thumbsup: I'll update customers once backfill completes and counts validated.

sarah (oncall): Incident status -> monitoring. If any regressions ping #incidents immediately. Good job team. :tada:
